events.title: Stephen Cook proves NP-completeness
events.summary: Stephen Cook published his theorem on NP-completeness in 1971 — defining the hardness class behind thousands of optimization problems.
events.about: Cook's work (and Karp's reductions) explained why many problems seem equally hard — shaping cryptography, scheduling, and complexity theory. P vs NP remains the field's defining open question.

narrative.whyChosen: NP-completeness is the central concept in computational complexity theory.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave a framework for identifying intractable problems in software and research.
narrative.problemSolved: There was no rigorous way to classify which problems were feasibly solvable.
